# Word Ladder (Bidirectional BFS)

Turn **cold** into **warm**, changing one letter at a time, every rung a real word. It's a shortest-path problem in disguise: words are nodes, one-letter edits are edges, BFS finds the shortest ladder.

The twist worth learning: BFS frontiers **grow roughly exponentially** with depth. Searching from both ends and meeting in the middle replaces one search of depth *d* with two of depth *d/2* — usually far fewer nodes.

Runs as ClojureScript in your browser, so it starts instantly.

(require '[clojure.string :as str])

(def words
  #{"cold" "cord" "card" "ward" "warm" "word" "worm" "wart" "want" "wand"
    "cool" "coal" "corn" "core" "care" "cart" "carp" "harp" "hard" "harm"
    "farm" "form" "fort" "sort" "sore" "bore" "bare" "bark" "dark" "dart"
    "mart" "mast" "most" "host" "hose" "nose" "note" "node" "code" "mode"
    "made" "mare" "more" "wore" "work" "tore" "torn" "turn" "burn" "born"
    "barn" "yarn" "earn" "ears" "eats" "oats" "oath" "bath" "bats" "rats"
    "raft" "rift" "gift" "girl" "gill" "will" "wall" "ball" "bald" "bold"})

(defn neighbors [w]
  (for [i (range 4)
        c "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
        :let [nw (str (subs w 0 i) c (subs w (inc i) 4))]
        :when (and (not= nw w) (contains? words nw))]
    nw))

;; --- one-way BFS, recording the frontier size at every level ----------
(defn bfs [start target]
  (loop [frontier #{start}
         parent {start nil}
         sizes []]
    (cond
      (contains? parent target)
      {:sizes sizes :parent parent :expanded (count parent)}

      (empty? frontier)
      {:sizes sizes :parent parent :expanded (count parent)}

      :else
      (let [pairs (for [w frontier, nw (neighbors w)
                        :when (not (contains? parent nw))] [nw w])
            parent' (reduce (fn [p [nw w]] (if (contains? p nw) p (assoc p nw w)))
                            parent pairs)
            frontier' (set (remove #(contains? parent %) (map first pairs)))]
        (recur frontier' parent' (conj sizes (count frontier)))))))

(defn path-of [parent w]
  (loop [w w, acc []]
    (if (nil? w) acc (recur (parent w) (cons w acc)))))

;; --- bidirectional: always expand the SMALLER frontier ----------------
(defn bidi [start target]
  (loop [fa #{start} pa {start nil}
         fb #{target} pb {target nil}
         sizes []]
    (let [meet (some fa fb)]
      (cond
        meet
        {:sizes sizes
         :expanded (+ (count pa) (count pb))
         :ladder (concat (path-of pa meet) (rest (reverse (path-of pb meet))))}

        (or (empty? fa) (empty? fb))
        {:sizes sizes :expanded (+ (count pa) (count pb)) :ladder nil}

        :else
        (let [[f p] (if (<= (count fa) (count fb)) [fa pa] [fb pb])
              pairs (for [w f, nw (neighbors w) :when (not (contains? p nw))] [nw w])
              p' (reduce (fn [m [nw w]] (if (contains? m nw) m (assoc m nw w))) p pairs)
              f' (set (remove #(contains? p %) (map first pairs)))]
          (if (<= (count fa) (count fb))
            (recur f' p' fb pb (conj sizes (count f)))
            (recur fa pa f' p' (conj sizes (count f)))))))))

(def one (bfs "cold" "warm"))
(def ladder (vec (path-of (:parent one) "warm")))
(def two (bidi "cold" "warm"))

(println "one-way ladder:" (str/join " -> " ladder))
(println "one-way explored" (:expanded one) "words, frontier sizes" (:sizes one))
(println "bidi ladder:   " (str/join " -> " (:ladder two)))
(println "bidi explored  " (:expanded two) "words, frontier sizes" (:sizes two))

(defn ja [xs] (str "[" (str/join "," xs) "]"))
(defn js [xs] (str "[" (str/join "," (map #(str "\"" % "\"") xs)) "]"))

(println (str "__NB_SET__ {\"key\":\"ladder\",\"value\":{"
              "\"ladder\":" (js ladder)
              ",\"oneway\":" (ja (:sizes one))
              ",\"bidi\":" (ja (:sizes two))
              ",\"onewayExpanded\":" (:expanded one)
              ",\"bidiExpanded\":" (:expanded two)
              ",\"words\":" (js (sort words)) "}}"))

## Reading the chart

One-way BFS's frontier keeps swelling until it happens to hit `warm`. The bidirectional line stays low: each side only reaches half the depth, and the search stops the moment the two footprints touch. On word graphs with fatter branching (real Scrabble dictionaries have ~25 neighbours per word) the gap becomes 10–100×.

## Try this

- Try `"bold"` → `"nose"` — a longer ladder; watch the frontier curves separate further.
- Delete `"cord"` **and** `"word"` from the dictionary — is there still a route? The BFS proves absence by running its frontier dry.
- Print *all* shortest ladders: keep a vector of parents per word instead of one, and walk every combination back.
- Bigger alphabet honesty check: the neighbour generator tries 26 letters × 4 positions = 104 candidates per word. Count how many are actual words on average (that's the branching factor of this graph).
